root_cause_label: Infinite null-byte probing loop instead of implementing compressor
one_sentence_failure_summary: After correctly understanding that a custom arithmetic-coded compressor was needed, the agent instead entered a ~160-step futile loop of feeding incremental null-byte sequences to the decompressor, exhausting its budget and ultimately submitting an incompatible gzip file.
t_err_evidence: Step 9: The agent runs 'echo "test" | /app/decomp' as a smoke test instead of starting to implement the compressor. Having correctly identified in step 7 that it needed to implement a range-encoder matching decomp.c, the agent instead begins probing the decompressor empirically with arbitrary inputs -- a strategy that cannot yield a valid compressed stream.
t_commit_evidence: By step 41 the agent has spent 30+ steps feeding arbitrary null-byte permutations to the decompressor (all producing segfaults) with no code written. The null-byte probing loop is firmly locked in and the remaining budget is insufficient to implement a real arithmetic encoder from scratch.
t_surface_evidence: Step 12: 'printf "\x00" | /app/decomp 2>&1' produces 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)' with exit code 139, the first observable signal that the probing strategy cannot produce a valid compressed stream.
trigger_explanation: The agent correctly articulated at step 7 that it needed to 'implement a compressor that matches the decompressor's expectations' but then acted on the false premise that empirically probing the decompressor with random bytes would reveal how to encode a valid stream. This assumption is incorrect: the custom range-coding scheme cannot be reverse-engineered by blind fuzzing, and no amount of null-byte trials can produce a valid compressed output.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 12-40: Every probe attempt results in a segmentation fault (exit code 139), a consistent command_error signal. Steps 15-40 show clearly repeated_command pattern where essentially the same null-byte sequences are fed again and again with only trivial length variations, indicating the strategy is not converging.
